version.changelog: Fix delivery step: add explicit Feishu API curl examples for container/server environments; add strict anti-pattern rules (never just output file path); support 3 delivery methods (OpenClaw tool / curl upload+send / file message fallback)

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (generate music and send to Feishu) but its instructions and code require sensitive credentials and runtime behaviors that are not declared in the registry metadata, and it includes automatic triggers for extreme emotional language without clear safety/consent controls.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (generate mood-matching music and send to Feishu) matches the code and instructions: they call a MiniMax music API/CLI and post audio to Feishu. However the package metadata declares no required environment variables or binaries while SKILL.md and scripts clearly require mmx-cli (or MINIMAX_API_KEY) and Feishu credentials (TENANT_ACCESS_TOKEN/CHAT_ID). That mismatch (metadata says 'none' but runtime needs API keys and CLI) is incoherent and should be fixed before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to monitor chat messages and automatically generate/send music on three trigger levels, including Level 3 auto-triggering on extreme emotional phrases (e.g., '活不下去', '崩溃了'). It also details local environment detection and playing files, and multiple delivery pathways (OpenClaw message tool, curl using TENANT_ACCESS_TOKEN, etc.). The instructions reference environment variables and chat IDs not declared in metadata and are vague about how to determine 'known users' or handle sensitive signals (no safety escalation or opt-out described).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only + a Python script). SKILL.md recommends installing mmx-cli via npm (user-run) which is a normal, low-friction step but not enforced by metadata. Because nothing is automatically downloaded or executed by the platform during install, install risk is low—however users must run npm install and ensure node/npm packages are legitimate.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime requires sensitive credentials (MINIMAX_API_KEY for the Python script; TENANT_ACCESS_TOKEN and CHAT_ID for Feishu API calls; mmx-cli auth may store keys) but the skill metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Requesting API keys for MiniMax and Feishu is proportionate to the stated functionality, but omitting them from the declared requirements is an inconsistency and increases risk (users may not realize the skill will use or ask for those tokens).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill can be invoked autonomously (default), which combined with the described Level 3 automatic triggers on sensitive/self-harm language increases potential for unexpected autonomous actions. The skill does not request elevated system-wide privileges or to modify other skills, but its auto-triggering behavior and lack of clear opt-in/consent/safety rules are noteworthy.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement what it claims, but it omits important runtime requirements and has potentially risky automatic behavior. Before installing: (1) Ask the publisher to update metadata to list required env vars (MINIMAX_API_KEY, TENANT_ACCESS_TOKEN, CHAT_ID) and required binaries (mmx-cli), and explain how tokens are stored/used. (2) Confirm Feishu token scopes are minimal (only file upload/send message) and do not expose broader tenant secrets. (3) Require an opt-in and an explicit configuration for automatic triggers (especially for Level 3). For sensitive/self-harm phrases, add safety handling (do not auto-respond—escalate to humans or hotlines, or require explicit consent). (4) Verify mmx-cli source (official repo) and cost/usage of the MiniMax token plan. (5) Test in a restricted/staging environment and review network calls (api.minimaxi.com and open.feishu.cn) and local playback behaviors before enabling in production. If the publisher cannot clarify/declares the required credentials and safety controls, treat the skill as untrusted.
